hook: SCP-1689 is a burlap sack of potatoes, and the joke is that it never runs out. The file is short and deadpan, so read the containment notes closely: the exception made for the site cooks is the first wink.
whyItMatters: It takes the idea of a mundane object with a bottomless inside and plays it for comedy with an edge of unease; its tags include both comedy and horror. A single absurd image, a sack you cannot empty, becomes the setup for a full expedition, though the mission log itself sits on a separate page rather than in the main file.
thingsToNotice: The tone shifts in the addendum about the Siberian village: about two hundred people who lived on the sack alone for more than a century turn out to be suffering severe calcium and iron deficiency, which gives a silly premise a sad undertow. The villagers cannot say where it came from, only that it predates the Soviets and was a reward for hard work, which hints at a giver the file never names. Small details build the scale, from regrowth that doubles every two hours to an enzyme compound developed just to push through the potatoes inside. A proposal to set up a mobile site inside a sack of potatoes is both very funny and faintly ominous.
